newsitem.title: FRANCE: French govt commissions study of car industry.
newsitem.headline: French govt commissions study of car industry.

text.p: The French Industry Ministry has commissioned a study on the impact of European Union regulations on the French car industry as part of a larger study on the European Union's industrial research policy.
The ministry said in a statement it had asked Henri Guillaume, honorary chairman of ANVAR, the state agency that promotes research, to head the study and submit a report by April.

"In an analysis focusing in particular on the European policy's influence on the car industry, he is expected to outline options offered by procedures and funds established by the Commission in research," the ministry said.
The study should also compare the French industry with those of other countries, including Korea, Japan and the United States, with special emphasis on R&D and labour.

The announcement follows a previous pledge by Industry Minister Franck Borotra to appoint another expert, Bernard Cabaret, to study a reported request by France's two carmakers to rejuvenate their workforces through 40,000 early retirements.
PSA Peugeot Citroen and Renault have not confirmed the request, which was reported in French newspapers.
The plan's cost to the French state is estimated at 30 billion francs, but the government has declined to confirm this.
The car companies have said they need to rejuvenate their staffs. The average age of workers at both companies is over 40, with Renault having the older workforce.
They say they have been steadily reducing their staffs -- to a combined 191,200 last year from over 300,000 in 1980 -- and have favoured early retirements to allow the hiring of young workers.

Borotra said in an interview this week with the newspaper Les Echos that the two companies need to study other ways to improve competitiveness than job cutbacks. He has been urging greater industrial cooperation among the two.
